metadata.description: Evaluation dataset for Legal RAG on Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (India)

queries.query: What is the maximum period a person can be detained without being produced before a Magistrate?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Twenty-four hours, excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the Magistrate's court.

queries.query: Who can arrest a person without a warrant?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any police officer may arrest without warrant any person who has been concerned in any cognizable offence, against whom a reasonable complaint or credible information has been received, or who is reasonably suspected.

queries.query: What is an FIR and which section deals with it?
queries.ground_truth_answer: FIR (First Information Report) is information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence given to an officer in charge of a police station, which shall be reduced to writing under Section 154.

queries.query: What are the different classes of criminal courts in India?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Courts of Session, Judicial Magistrates of the first class and second class, Executive Magistrates, and in metropolitan areas, Metropolitan Magistrates.

queries.query: What is the maximum sentence a Judicial Magistrate of the first class can impose?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees, or both.

queries.query: Who appoints the Public Prosecutor?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The State Government shall appoint a Public Prosecutor for conducting prosecution in the High Court and for every district.

queries.query: What is the procedure for recording confessions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate may record any confession or statement made to him in the course of an investigation, after warning the person that they are not bound to make a confession.

queries.query: How is a summons served on an individual?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A summons shall be served by a police officer or court officer by delivering or tendering a duplicate of the summons to the person summoned personally.

queries.query: What is the duration of a warrant of arrest?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A warrant of arrest shall remain in force until it is cancelled by the Court which issued it, or until it is executed.

queries.query: When can a search warrant be issued?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where any Court has reason to believe that a person will not produce a document or thing as required by summons, or where such document or thing is not known to be in possession of any person.

queries.query: What is the time limit for completing investigation in cases punishable with death or life imprisonment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Ninety days from the date of detention where the offence is punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than ten years. For all other cognizable offences the period is sixty days. If the chargesheet is not filed within the applicable period the accused becomes entitled to bail as of right under the proviso to Section 167(2).

queries.query: What is the power of a Magistrate to order maintenance of wives, children and parents?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate of the first class may order the husband of a wife who is unable to maintain herself, or the father or mother of a child or parent who is unable to maintain themselves, to pay a monthly allowance for maintenance at such monthly rate as such Magistrate thinks fit. The statute does not prescribe a maximum amount; the Magistrate exercises judicial discretion based on the means of the payer and the needs of the claimant.

queries.query: Who can compound offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The person against whom the offence was committed may compound it, with or without the permission of the Court depending on the nature of the offence.

queries.query: What is the limitation period for taking cognizance of an offence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Six months for offences punishable with fine only, one year for offences punishable with imprisonment up to one year, three years for offences punishable with imprisonment between one and three years.

queries.query: What happens when an accused person absconds?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may publish a written proclamation requiring the accused to appear at a specified place and time, not less than thirty days from the publication.

queries.query: Who can grant pardon to an accomplice?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Chief Judicial Magistrate or Metropolitan Magistrate may tender a pardon to any person supposed to have been directly or indirectly concerned in or privy to an offence.

queries.query: What is the court's power to direct identification of a person arrested?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 54A provides that where a person is arrested and is required to be identified for the purpose of investigation, the Court having jurisdiction may on the request of the officer in charge of the police station direct that identification of the person be done in such manner as the Court considers fit. The Court may also direct that the identification of a witness be made in conditions which ensure the witness cannot be seen by the person being identified.

queries.query: What are the rights of an arrested person?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The arrested person has the right to know the grounds of arrest, to be informed about right to bail, and to meet an advocate of their choice during interrogation.

queries.query: What is the definition of cognizable offence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A cognizable offence means an offence for which a police officer may arrest without warrant in accordance with the First Schedule.

queries.query: What is the procedure for medical examination of a rape victim?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The examination shall be conducted by a registered medical practitioner with the consent of the victim or a person competent to give such consent.

queries.query: How long can police custody be granted?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate may authorize detention in police custody for a term not exceeding fifteen days in the whole.

queries.query: What is the procedure for execution of a sentence of death?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The sentence of death shall not be executed until it has been confirmed by the High Court. Section 413 provides that when a sentence of death is passed by a Court of Session it shall be submitted to the High Court for confirmation. Section 414 provides that the High Court may confirm the sentence or pass any other sentence warranted by law. The warrant of execution is issued only after confirmation by the High Court.

queries.query: What is the power of police to investigate?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any officer in charge of a police station may investigate any cognizable case without the order of a Magistrate.

queries.query: What is the law on registration of information in cognizable cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, read over to the informant, and signed by the informant. The substance shall be entered in a book kept by such officer in the prescribed form. A copy shall be given free of cost to the informant. The section does not restrict registration to the station within whose jurisdiction the offence occurred.

queries.query: What is the charge sheet and when is it filed?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The police officer shall forward a report (charge sheet) to the Magistrate upon completion of investigation, stating whether an offence appears to have been committed.

queries.query: What is the procedure for trial of warrant cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In warrant cases instituted on police report, the Magistrate shall consider the police report and documents, and may discharge the accused if no sufficient ground exists.

queries.query: What is the difference between summons case and warrant case?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Summons case means a case relating to an offence punishable with imprisonment for not more than two years. Warrant case means a case relating to an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for more than two years.

queries.query: Who can withdraw a prosecution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Public Prosecutor may, with the consent of the Court, withdraw from prosecution of any person either generally or in respect of any one or more of the offences.

queries.query: What is the power of High Court to transfer cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court may transfer any case or appeal from one Criminal Court subordinate to it to any other such Court of equal or superior jurisdiction.

queries.query: What is plea bargaining?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A person accused of an offence punishable with imprisonment up to seven years may file an application for plea bargaining in the Court where the trial is pending.

queries.query: What is the procedure when investigation cannot be completed in 24 hours?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The officer shall transmit to the nearest Judicial Magistrate a copy of the entries in the case diary and forward the accused to such Magistrate.

queries.query: What is Section 144 order?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A District Magistrate or Executive Magistrate may issue an order directing any person to abstain from a certain act to prevent obstruction, annoyance, danger to human life, or disturbance of public tranquillity.

queries.query: What is the inherent power of High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Nothing in the Code shall limit or affect the inherent powers of the High Court to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order, or to prevent abuse of process, or to secure the ends of justice.

queries.query: What is the time limit for filing an appeal against conviction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Appeals shall be filed within the period of limitation prescribed by law, generally thirty days from the date of judgment.

queries.query: What are the conditions for granting anticipatory bail?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may impose conditions such as making oneself available for interrogation, not making any inducement or threat to witnesses, not leaving India without permission, and other conditions as deemed fit.

queries.query: What are the grounds for refusing bail in non-bailable offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Bail may be refused if there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is guilty of an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment, or if the accused is previously convicted of a similar offence, or likely to commit another offence, or tamper with evidence.

queries.query: What obligations does a police officer have when making an arrest?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The officer must bear accurate identification, prepare a memorandum of arrest attested by a family member or respectable person, inform the arrested person of grounds of arrest and right to bail, and make entry in a register.

queries.query: Under what circumstances can a confession be considered valid?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A confession must be recorded by a Metropolitan or Judicial Magistrate, with the person warned they are not bound to confess, made voluntarily without police presence, and the Magistrate must be satisfied it is being made voluntarily.

queries.query: What protections exist for women during arrest?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No woman shall be arrested after sunset and before sunrise except in exceptional circumstances with prior permission from Judicial Magistrate. Search of a woman must be made by another woman with strict regard to decency.

queries.query: What are the requirements for a valid search warrant?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The warrant must be in writing, signed by the issuing officer, specify the thing to be searched for, and the search must be conducted during daytime unless the warrant authorizes night search.

queries.query: What rights does an accused have during examination by the court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The accused shall be questioned without oath, shall not render himself liable to punishment for refusing to answer or giving false answers, and the answers may be taken into consideration.

queries.query: What are the conditions for granting maintenance to a wife?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A wife is entitled to maintenance if she is unable to maintain herself, has not committed adultery, is not living separately by mutual consent, and has no refused to live with her husband without sufficient reason.

queries.query: What are the powers of the Court of Session regarding bail?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court or Court of Session may direct that any person be released on bail, impose any condition it considers necessary, and may cancel bail already granted if conditions are violated.

queries.query: What factors should be considered before issuing an order under Section 144?
queries.ground_truth_answer: There must be sufficient ground for proceeding, cases of urgency, likelihood of causing obstruction or annoyance or injury to persons, danger to human life or safety, or disturbance of public tranquillity.

queries.query: What are the conditions for tender of pardon to an accomplice?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The pardon may be tendered on condition of making full and true disclosure of all circumstances within knowledge. If the person fails to comply, they may be tried for the original offence and also for giving false evidence.

queries.query: What are the requirements for a valid complaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate shall examine the complainant and witnesses on oath, may postpone issue of process and direct investigation, and shall dismiss the complaint if there is no sufficient ground for proceeding.

queries.query: What are the provisions for compensation to victims?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may order the accused to pay compensation to the victim for any loss or injury. The State Government shall prepare a scheme for compensation to victims who have suffered loss and require rehabilitation.

queries.query: What are the grounds for revision of a judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court or Sessions Judge may call for and examine the record of any proceeding for the purpose of satisfying itself as to the correctness, legality, or propriety of any finding, sentence, or order.

queries.query: What are the duties of police on receiving information about cognizable offence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The officer shall reduce the information to writing, read it to the informant, get it signed, enter the substance in a book, forthwith send a report to the Magistrate, and proceed to investigate.

queries.query: Under what conditions can a case be tried summarily?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Offences punishable with imprisonment up to two years may be tried summarily by a Chief Judicial Magistrate or Metropolitan Magistrate, provided no sentence of imprisonment exceeding three months shall be passed.

queries.query: What are the provisions for protection of members of Armed Forces from arrest?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Members of Armed Forces cannot be arrested for anything done in discharge of official duties except after obtaining consent of the Central Government.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for sanction to prosecute a public servant?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No Court shall take cognizance of an offence alleged to have been committed by a public servant while acting in discharge of official duty, except with prior sanction from the appropriate Government.

queries.query: What are the requirements for framing of charge?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The charge shall state the offence with particulars of time and place, the person against whom or thing with respect to which the offence was committed, and be in writing and explained to the accused.

queries.query: What are the provisions for joint trials?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Persons accused of the same offence, persons accused of different offences committed in the same transaction, or persons accused of offences involving stolen property may be tried together.

queries.query: What are the rules regarding examination of witnesses?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Evidence shall be taken in presence of the accused, or when personal attendance is dispensed with, in presence of the pleader. The evidence shall be recorded in the language of the Court.

queries.query: What constitutes a valid judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The judgment shall be delivered in open Court, contain the point for determination, decision thereon, and reasons for the decision. If conviction, it shall specify the offence and punishment.

queries.query: What are the provisions for default bail?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If investigation is not completed within 60 days (for offences punishable up to 10 years) or 90 days (for offences punishable with death, life imprisonment, or more than 10 years), the accused shall be released on bail.

queries.query: What are the grounds for quashing of FIR?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court may quash an FIR to prevent abuse of process of law, when allegations do not constitute an offence, when there is legal bar to proceeding, or to secure ends of justice.

queries.query: What are the powers of police regarding seized property?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The police may seize property suspected to be stolen or found under suspicious circumstances. The Court may make an order for custody, delivery, sale, or destruction of such property.

queries.query: What are the provisions for trial in absentia?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Personal attendance of the accused may be dispensed with if the accused is represented by a pleader and is not required for identification. The trial may proceed in the absence of the accused.

queries.query: What are the grounds for rejection of a complaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate may dismiss the complaint if, after considering the statements and result of inquiry, there is no sufficient ground for proceeding.

queries.query: What are the provisions for attachment of property of an absconding person?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may order attachment of property of the proclaimed person. Claims may be made within six months. The property may be sold if the person does not appear within two years.

queries.query: What are the conditions for recording dying declaration?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A dying declaration may be recorded by a Magistrate or any person when the person is in expectation of death. It must be recorded as nearly as possible in the words of the dying person.

queries.query: What are the provisions for security for keeping peace?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When a person is convicted of certain offences, the Court may order them to execute a bond for keeping peace. If information is received about likelihood of breach of peace, a Magistrate may require security.

queries.query: What are the rights of victims during trial?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The victim has the right to engage an advocate, to be heard in bail and compensation matters, and to receive compensation from the State Victim Compensation Fund.

queries.query: What are the provisions for police report after investigation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Upon completion of investigation, the officer shall forward a report stating whether any offence appears committed, names of parties, nature of information, and whether the accused is in custody or released on bail.

queries.query: What are the provisions for discharge of accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If upon consideration of the record and documents, the Judge considers that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, he shall discharge the accused and record reasons.

queries.query: How does Section 167 detention relate to the 24-hour rule in Section 57?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 57 requires production before Magistrate within 24 hours. Section 167 comes into play when investigation cannot be completed within this period, allowing the Magistrate to authorize further detention.

queries.query: What is the relationship between FIR under Section 154 and investigation powers under Section 156?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 154 deals with recording of FIR for cognizable offences. Once FIR is registered, Section 156 empowers the police officer to investigate the cognizable case without Magistrate's order.

queries.query: How do bail provisions in Section 437 interact with Section 439?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 437 deals with bail by Magistrates in non-bailable offences with restrictions. Section 439 gives wider powers to High Court and Sessions Court including power to cancel bail granted under Section 437.

queries.query: How does anticipatory bail under Section 438 relate to regular bail under Section 437?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 438 provides for bail before arrest in anticipation of arrest for non-bailable offence. Section 437 applies after arrest. If anticipatory bail is granted, Section 437 restrictions may not apply.

queries.query: What is the connection between arrest under Section 41 and the duties under Section 41B?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 41 specifies when police can arrest without warrant. Section 41B mandates the procedure and duties during such arrest including wearing visible identification and preparing arrest memo.

queries.query: How does the complaint procedure in Section 200 relate to Section 156(3)?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Under Section 200, Magistrate examines complainant on oath. However, under Section 156(3), a Magistrate can direct the police to investigate a cognizable offence instead of examining the complainant.

queries.query: What is the relationship between police investigation under Section 173 and the trial court proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 173 report is forwarded to Magistrate who takes cognizance under Section 190. Based on this, the Magistrate may issue process under Section 204 to commence trial.

queries.query: How does Section 313 examination relate to the evidence recorded under Section 275?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 275 provides for recording of evidence. Section 313 requires the Court to question the accused about the evidence recorded against him, allowing explanation of incriminating circumstances.

queries.query: What is the connection between confession under Section 164 and statements under Section 161?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 161 deals with police examination of witnesses which cannot be used as substantive evidence. Section 164 confession before Magistrate is admissible. Section 162 bars use of Section 161 statements.

queries.query: How does the revision power under Section 397 interact with inherent powers under Section 482?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 397 provides revisional jurisdiction with certain limitations. Section 482 preserves inherent powers which can be exercised even where Section 397 is barred, but should be exercised sparingly.

queries.query: What is the relationship between charge framing under Section 228 and discharge under Section 227?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 227 provides for discharge if no sufficient ground exists. If the Judge does not discharge under Section 227, he shall frame charge under Section 228 when there is ground for presuming the accused has committed the offence.

queries.query: How does Section 125 maintenance relate to Section 127 alteration of allowance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 125 provides for initial maintenance order. Section 127 allows the Magistrate to alter or cancel the order on proof of change in circumstances of any party.

queries.query: What is the connection between proclamation under Section 82 and attachment under Section 83?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 82 provides for proclamation when accused absconds. Section 83 empowers attachment of property of the proclaimed person if they fail to appear within the time specified in the proclamation.

queries.query: How does Section 436 mandatory bail relate to the restrictions in Section 437?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 436 mandates release on bail for bailable offences as a matter of right. Section 437 deals with non-bailable offences where bail is discretionary and subject to various conditions and restrictions.

queries.query: What is the relationship between appeal under Section 374 and revision under Section 397?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 374 provides right of appeal against conviction. Section 397 provides revisional jurisdiction where appeal may not lie or has been filed. However, Section 397(3) bars revision during pendency of appeal.

queries.query: How does the warrant case procedure under Section 238 connect with charge framing under Section 240?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 238 provides for compliance with Section 207 in warrant cases on police report. If not discharged under Section 239, the Magistrate frames charge under Section 240.

queries.query: What is the connection between compounding under Section 320 and withdrawal under Section 321?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 320 allows victim to compound certain offences leading to acquittal. Section 321 allows Public Prosecutor to withdraw prosecution with court consent. Both result in termination but through different parties.

queries.query: How does prosecution sanction under Section 197 relate to cognizance under Section 190?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 190 provides for taking cognizance of offences. Section 197 restricts cognizance of offences by public servants unless prior sanction is obtained from the appropriate government.

queries.query: What is the relationship between the sentence by Sessions Court and confirmation by High Court under Section 366?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When Sessions Court passes death sentence under its powers, Section 366 mandates submission of proceedings to High Court for confirmation. Section 368 provides for powers of High Court in confirmation.

queries.query: How does the power to summon additional evidence under Section 311 relate to examination under Section 313?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 311 allows court to summon any witness at any stage. If new evidence is summoned after Section 313 examination, the accused must be given opportunity to explain it through further Section 313 questioning.

queries.query: What is the connection between Section 144 orders and judicial review under Section 144A?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 144 empowers Magistrate to issue prohibitory orders. Section 144A empowers State Government to prohibit carrying arms in public procession. Appeals against Section 144 lie with State Government.

queries.query: How does the inquiry procedure under Section 202 relate to dismissal under Section 203?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 202 provides for postponement of issue of process and inquiry. Section 203 empowers dismissal of complaint if after considering Section 200 examination and Section 202 inquiry, there is no sufficient ground.

queries.query: What is the relationship between custody under Section 167 and default bail under proviso?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 167(2) proviso creates an indefeasible right to bail if investigation is not completed within 60/90 days as applicable. This is called statutory or default bail and arises from the same section's time limits.

queries.query: How does further investigation under Section 173(8) relate to supplementary charge sheet?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 173(2) provides for initial report. Section 173(8) permits further investigation after filing charge sheet, resulting in supplementary or additional charge sheet being filed with new evidence or accused.

queries.query: What is the connection between special jurisdiction of courts under Section 26 and transfer of cases under Section 407?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 26 specifies which courts can try which offences. Section 407 allows High Court to transfer cases to courts of equal or superior jurisdiction, respecting the jurisdictional limits set by Section 26.

queries.query: How does Section 164 confession to Magistrate differ from Section 281 record of examination by Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 164 deals with confessions during investigation recorded by Magistrate. Section 281 deals with examination of accused during trial. Both require similar safeguards but at different stages.

queries.query: What is the relationship between police custody remand and judicial custody under Section 167?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Under Section 167(2), police custody can be for maximum 15 days. After that, the accused must be remanded to judicial custody. Total detention cannot exceed 60/90 days before default bail right accrues.

queries.query: How does Section 41A notice relate to Section 41 arrest provisions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 41 provides for arrest without warrant. Section 41A introduced requirement to issue notice of appearance before arrest in less serious cases, as an alternative to arrest where detention is not necessary.

queries.query: What is the connection between plea bargaining application under Section 265A and sentence under Section 265E?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 265A permits application for plea bargaining. If the court accepts and follows the procedure, Section 265E provides for the judgment awarding sentence of one-fourth of minimum or half of fixed punishment.

queries.query: How does Section 357 compensation on conviction relate to Section 357A victim compensation scheme?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 357 empowers court to order accused to pay compensation upon conviction. Section 357A creates State Victim Compensation Scheme for cases where compensation under Section 357 is inadequate or where offender is not traced or identified.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Section 154 FIR and Section 155 for non-cognizable offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 154 deals with information about cognizable offences which police must register and investigate. Section 155 deals with non-cognizable offences where police can only investigate with Magistrate's order.

queries.query: How does the power of remand under Section 309 relate to custody under Section 167?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 167 applies during investigation before cognizance. Section 309 applies after cognizance is taken, allowing remand from time to time during trial. The time limits and purposes differ.

queries.query: What is the connection between discharge under Section 245 in summons cases and acquittal under Section 255?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In summons cases, Section 245 allows discharge if no case is made out after prosecution evidence. Section 255 provides for acquittal after full trial if offence is not proved. Discharge is earlier stage than acquittal.

queries.query: What is the procedure when an accused person is of unsound mind?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The inquiry shall be postponed and the accused shall be sent to a lunatic asylum or other safe custody until competent to make his defence.

queries.query: What is the power of High Court to transfer cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court may transfer any case or appeal from one Criminal Court to another, if it is expedient for the ends of justice.

queries.query: What is the provision for legal aid to accused at state expense?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where the accused is not represented by a pleader and the Court is of opinion that the circumstances of the case and the interests of justice require, the Court shall assign a pleader at State expense.

queries.query: What is the power of Magistrate to disperse an unlawful assembly?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The executive Magistrate may command any unlawful or riotous assembly to disperse and may use civil force to disperse it if it does not disperse.

queries.query: How is a charge framed in a Sessions trial?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If after hearing arguments the Judge is of opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed an offence, the Judge shall frame a charge in writing against the accused.

queries.query: What is the power to try summarily?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Chief Judicial Magistrate, Metropolitan Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class may try certain offences summarily, including theft where property value does not exceed two thousand rupees.

queries.query: What is a charge under CrPC?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A charge shall contain the offence with which the accused is charged stated as distinctly as the nature of the case admits, including the specific section of the penal law.

queries.query: What is the power to postpone proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Court may postpone the commencement of any inquiry or trial, or adjourn any inquiry or trial that has commenced, to a future day for reasons to be recorded.

queries.query: What is the procedure after charge is framed in warrant cases by Magistrate?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When a charge is framed the Magistrate shall read and explain the charge to the accused and ask whether he pleads guilty or wishes to be tried.

queries.query: What is anticipatory bail?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When any person has reason to believe that they may be arrested on an accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence, they may apply to the High Court or Sessions Court for a direction for bail.

queries.query: What is the power to commute sentence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The appropriate Government may commute death sentence to rigorous imprisonment for life, and any sentence of imprisonment to a lesser term.

queries.query: What is the power to suspend or remit sentences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The appropriate Government may suspend the execution of a sentence or remit the whole or any part of the punishment to which a person has been sentenced.

queries.query: Who is a Public Prosecutor?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Public Prosecutor means any person appointed under Section 24 and includes any person acting under the directions of a Public Prosecutor.

queries.query: What is the power of Court to examine accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may at any stage of an inquiry or trial examine the accused for the purpose of enabling the accused to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidence against them.

queries.query: What is the procedure for compounding of offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Offences specified in the first column may be compounded by the persons specified in the second column with or without permission of the Court.

queries.query: What are the provisions for protection of witnesses?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Threatening any person to give false evidence or to desist from making a complaint may be punished as contempt of court.

queries.query: What is the right of accused to be defended by a pleader?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any person accused of an offence before a Criminal Court has the right to be defended by a pleader of his choice.

queries.query: What is the procedure for disposal of property in conclusion of trial?
queries.ground_truth_answer: At the conclusion of an inquiry or trial, the Court may make an order for the disposal of any property produced before it.

queries.query: What is commitment to Court of Session?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When the accused appears before a Magistrate and the offence is exclusively triable by the Court of Session, the Magistrate shall commit the case to the Court of Session.

queries.query: What is the power of Court regarding bail pending appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A convicted person filing an appeal may apply for suspension of sentence pending the appeal; the Court may order the convicted person to be released on bail.

queries.query: What is the procedure for investigation of cognizable offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If from information received or otherwise, an officer in charge of a police station has reason to suspect the commission of a cognizable offence, they shall proceed to the spot to investigate.

queries.query: What is an inquest under Section 174?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When the officer in charge of a police station receives information that a person has committed suicide or been killed by another, they shall immediately give intimation to the nearest Executive Magistrate.

queries.query: What is the definition of bailable and non-bailable offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A bailable offence is one shown as bailable in the First Schedule; a non-bailable offence means any other offence.

queries.query: What is the procedure for summoning and examining witness?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Court may at any stage of any inquiry trial or other proceeding summon any person as a witness and examine any person in attendance even if not summoned as a witness.

queries.query: What is the inherent power of High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Nothing in the Code shall be deemed to limit or affect the inherent powers of the High Court to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order or to prevent abuse of process.

queries.query: What is the power of revision by High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In the case of any proceeding in the Sessions Court, the High Court may exercise all or any of the powers conferred on a Court of Appeal by Sections 386, 389, 390 and 391.

queries.query: What is the procedure for withdrawal from prosecution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Public Prosecutor may with the consent of the Court withdraw from the prosecution of any person at any time before judgment is pronounced.

queries.query: What is the limitation for filing appeal by State against acquittal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The State Government may direct the Public Prosecutor to present an appeal to the High Court against an order of acquittal; leave of the High Court is required.

queries.query: What are the provisions for compensation to victims of crime?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may order a portion of fine to be paid as compensation to any person for loss or injury caused by the offence.

queries.query: What is the procedure for examination of complainant?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate taking cognizance of an offence on complaint shall examine upon oath the complainant and the witnesses present.

queries.query: What is the procedure when Magistrate cannot pass sufficient sentence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When a Magistrate is of opinion that the case is one that should be dealt with by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, he shall transmit the case to the Chief Judicial Magistrate.

queries.query: What is the power to search in exigencies?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A police officer making an investigation may search any place within the limits of the station without a warrant if they have reasonable grounds to believe that delay would be detrimental.

queries.query: What is the procedure regarding hostile witness?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If a witness appears to be hostile the prosecution may apply to examine the witness on the statement previously made, and the Court may permit cross-examination by the party who called them.

queries.query: What are the provisions for witness protection?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Except as otherwise expressly provided, all evidence taken in the course of trial shall be taken in the presence of the accused or his pleader.

queries.query: What is the procedure for disposal of case at first hearing in warrant cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If upon considering the police report and the documents the Magistrate considers the charge against the accused groundless, the Magistrate shall discharge the accused.

queries.query: What is the procedure for bond and bail?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Before any person is released on bail, a bond shall be executed by such person and also by his sureties for the sum and conditions specified.

queries.query: What is double jeopardy under CrPC?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A person once convicted or acquitted for an offence shall not be liable to be tried again for the same offence or on the same facts.

queries.query: What is the procedure for taking cognizance on complaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Magistrate may take cognizance of an offence upon receiving a complaint of facts which constitute such offence, or upon a police report, or upon information received from any person.

queries.query: What is the power of Court to order local inspection?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Judge or Magistrate may inspect any place connected with any case pending before it at any time before judgment.

queries.query: What is the procedure for attachment of property of absconder?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If a person fails to appear in answer to a proclamation, the Court may order attachment of any property belonging to such person.

queries.query: What are executive magistrate's powers under Section 144?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In urgent cases of apprehended danger, a District Magistrate or Sub-divisional Magistrate may order any person to abstain from a certain act or to take certain order with certain property.

queries.query: When must copies of documents be supplied to accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In any case where a police report has been filed, the Magistrate shall without delay furnish the accused free of cost with a copy of the police report and other relevant documents.

queries.query: What is the procedure for recording evidence in absence of accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If it is proved that an accused person has absconded and there is no immediate prospect of arresting him, the Court may take evidence of any witness.

queries.query: What is the provision for security for good behaviour from habitual offenders?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate may order a person convicted of an offence to execute a bond for good behaviour for a period not exceeding three years.

queries.query: What are the provisions for maintenance of wife?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate of the first class may order the husband of a wife who is unable to maintain herself to pay a monthly allowance.

queries.query: What is the procedure when there is dispute concerning land?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Whenever an Executive Magistrate is satisfied from a report of a police officer or other information that a dispute likely to cause a breach of peace exists concerning land, the Magistrate shall issue an order.

queries.query: What is the procedure for forfeiture of bond?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a bond for appearance or good behaviour has been forfeited, the Magistrate shall record the grounds of such order and call upon each person bound thereby to show cause why they should not pay the penalty.

queries.query: What is the power to hold trial in camera?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court of Session and every Court of a Magistrate may hold inquiry or trial in camera if satisfied that the interests of justice so require.

queries.query: What is the procedure for reference to High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a Court is of opinion that the case involves a question of law which requires decision, it may refer the same to the High Court.

queries.query: What is the procedure for appeal from Sessions Judge's order?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any person convicted on a trial held by a Sessions Judge or a Metropolitan Magistrate may appeal to the High Court.

queries.query: What is the power of appellate court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Appellate Court may reverse the finding, sentence or order appealed against, enhance or reduce the sentence, or alter the nature of the sentence.

queries.query: What is the definition of inquiry under CrPC?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Inquiry means every inquiry other than a trial conducted under the Code by a Magistrate or Court.

queries.query: What is the procedure for grant of bail in bailable offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When any person accused of a bailable offence is arrested, they shall be released on bail if they are prepared to give bail.

queries.query: Who can cancel bail?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Court which has granted bail may, if it considers it necessary, direct that any person be arrested and committed to custody.

queries.query: What is the special power of High Court regarding bail?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court or Court of Session may direct that any person be released on bail, may impose conditions, or may set aside or modify conditions imposed by a Magistrate.

queries.query: What is the procedure for tender of pardon?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Chief Judicial Magistrate may tender a pardon to any person supposed to be directly or indirectly concerned in the offence, on the condition of making a full and true disclosure.

queries.query: What is the procedure when investigation cannot be completed in time?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When the case is not completed within the period of investigation the Magistrate may authorize detention in judicial custody for a total period not exceeding 60 or 90 days.

queries.query: What is the procedure for maintenance of children?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate may order father or mother of a legitimate or illegitimate child unable to maintain itself to pay monthly allowance for maintenance.

queries.query: What is the procedure for medical examination of accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When a person is arrested, the police officer shall arrange for examination of the arrested person by a medical officer if the person or his relative requests.

queries.query: What are provisions relating to probation of good conduct?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may release an offender on probation of good conduct if convicted of an offence not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.

queries.query: What is the procedure for issue of process on complaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If in the opinion of a Magistrate taking cognizance of an offence there is sufficient ground for proceeding, the Magistrate shall issue a summons or warrant for the attendance of the accused.

queries.query: What is the procedure for framing of charge in warrant cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If after hearing the prosecution and examination of the accused the Magistrate is of opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed an offence, the Magistrate shall frame a charge.

queries.query: What is the power to call for records of lower court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court or Sessions Court may call for and examine the record of any proceeding before any inferior Criminal Court for the purpose of satisfying itself as to the correctness of any finding.

queries.query: What is the procedure for examination of witnesses by police?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any police officer making an investigation may examine orally any person supposed to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case.

queries.query: What is the law on statements to police?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No statement made by any person to a police officer in the course of investigation shall be signed by the person making it; nor shall any such statement be used as evidence.

queries.query: What are the powers of Sessions Judge in sentencing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Sessions Judge or Additional Sessions Judge may pass any sentence authorised by law; but any sentence of death shall be subject to confirmation by the High Court.

queries.query: What is the procedure for identification of accused by witnesses?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a person is arrested for commission of an offence and the Court thinks it expedient, it may direct identification of the accused by any person in such manner as the Court may direct.

queries.query: What is the procedure for committal proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When an accused appears before a Magistrate for an offence exclusively triable by the Court of Session, the Magistrate shall commit the case to the Court of Session.

queries.query: What is the power to transfer cases by Supreme Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Supreme Court may transfer any case or appeal from one High Court to another, or from a Criminal Court in one State to another, where it is expedient for the ends of justice.

queries.query: What is the procedure for maintenance of parents?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate may order a person to pay monthly allowance for maintenance of his father or mother who is unable to maintain themselves.

queries.query: What is a non-cognizable offence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A non-cognizable offence is one for which a police officer has no authority to arrest without warrant according to the First Schedule.

queries.query: What is the procedure for disposal of case on plea of guilty in warrant case?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If the accused pleads guilty to a charge framed in a warrant case trial, the Judge shall record the plea and may convict the accused thereon.

queries.query: What is the procedure for appeal by the State against sentence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The State Government may direct the Public Prosecutor to present an appeal to the Court of Session against the sentence passed by a Magistrate on the ground that it is inadequate.

queries.query: What is the effect of omission to frame or error in charge?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No finding, sentence or order shall be deemed invalid merely on the ground that no charge was framed or that there was an error or omission in the charge, unless a failure of justice was occasioned thereby.

queries.query: What is the power to grant bail where trial is delayed?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If in any case involving non-bailable offence the trial is not concluded in sixty days the accused shall be released on bail by default.

queries.query: What is the procedure for search by Magistrate?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where any Court has reason to believe that a person to whom a summons or order for production has been addressed will not produce the document, the Court may issue a search warrant.

queries.query: What is the procedure for proclamation before attachment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Court may issue a proclamation requiring a person to appear before it if it has reason to believe that the person has absconded or is concealing themselves.

queries.query: What is the period of limitation for certain offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The period of limitation shall commence on the date of the offence, or where the commission of the offence was not known to the aggrieved party, from when it first came to knowledge.

queries.query: What is the procedure for release of person on bail?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The amount of every bond executed shall be fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case and shall not be excessive.

queries.query: What are the provisions for protection from groundless arrest?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Whoever causes a police officer to arrest any person without sufficient grounds shall pay compensation to the person arrested.

queries.query: What is the procedure for security for keeping the peace?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate may require any person to show cause why they should not be ordered to execute a bond for keeping the peace for a period not exceeding one year.

queries.query: What is the procedure for a summary trial judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In every case tried summarily the Magistrate shall record the substance of the evidence and a judgment containing a brief statement of reasons.

queries.query: What is the power of Court in revision not to convert acquittal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In the exercise of its powers of revision the High Court shall not convert a finding of acquittal into one of conviction.

queries.query: What are the provisions for witness expenses?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Subject to any rules made by the State Government, the reasonable expenses of every witness attending for the purpose of any inquiry shall be paid to the witness.

queries.query: What is the procedure for disposal of property seized by police?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The police officer seizing any property shall place it in safe custody and make a report to the Magistrate within the jurisdiction within whose jurisdiction the property was seized.

queries.query: What is meant by irregularities that vitiate proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If a Magistrate, not being empowered by law to do so, tries an offender or commits the same for trial, such irregularities shall vitiate the proceedings.

queries.query: What is the procedure for security for good behaviour from persons disseminating seditious matter?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Whenever a Magistrate is informed that any person publishes seditious material, the Magistrate may require such person to show cause why they should not be ordered to execute a bond.

queries.query: What is the duty of police to prevent cognizable offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every police officer may interpose for the purpose of preventing and shall prevent the commission of any cognizable offence.

queries.query: What is the procedure for discharge in warrant cases instituted on complaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If at any stage of the trial in a complaint case the Magistrate finds that no case has been made out which if unrebutted would warrant conviction, the Magistrate shall discharge the accused.

queries.query: What is the procedure for acquittal in complaint cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When in a complaint case the accused is acquitted, the Magistrate shall consider whether the complainant ought to be ordered to pay compensation to the accused.

queries.query: What are the powers of Magistrate to make order for removal of nuisance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A District Magistrate or Sub-divisional Magistrate may make a conditional order requiring a person to remove a public nuisance within a fixed time.

queries.query: What is the procedure for inquiry into disputed land?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If in the Magistrate's opinion there is a case of emergency or apprehension of breach of peace, the Magistrate shall attach the subject of dispute and keep it in custody.

queries.query: What are the provisions for compensation in cases of false accusation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If a Magistrate makes a complaint under Section 195 or discharges an accused person, the Magistrate shall consider whether the complainant should pay compensation.

queries.query: What is the power of Appellate Court to take additional evidence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In dealing with any appeal, the Appellate Court may, if it thinks additional evidence to be necessary, record the same itself.

queries.query: What are the provisions for remission of sentences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The appropriate Government may without conditions or upon conditions remit the whole or any part of the punishment to which the person has been sentenced.

queries.query: What is a Metropolitan Magistrate?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Metropolitan Magistrate means a Magistrate appointed for a metropolitan area under Section 16.

queries.query: What is the power to set aside ex parte order?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If an accused appears after expiry of the time fixed for their appearance and satisfactorily accounts for their absence, the Court may recall witnesses and proceed as if the accused had not been absent.

queries.query: What is the procedure for appeal against order of maintenance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The order of maintenance may be altered or cancelled by the Magistrate if the husband can show change in circumstances.

queries.query: What is the procedure in cases of proclamation of absconder?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A proclamation shall be published in some newspaper circulating in the locality stating that the person named therein is required to appear.

queries.query: What is the power of High Court to make supplementary rules?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every High Court may make rules consistent with the Code for all or any of the purposes therein specified.

queries.query: What is the procedure for non-appearance of complainant?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If the summons has been issued on complaint and the complainant does not appear, the Magistrate shall acquit the accused unless for reasons to be recorded it adjourns the hearing.

queries.query: What is the provision for protection of identity of the victim of certain offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 228A prohibits printing or publishing the name or any matter which may make known the identity of any person against whom an offence under Sections 376, 376A, 376B, 376C or 376D is alleged or found to have been committed. The prohibition applies in relation to any proceeding before any Court unless the Court permits disclosure in the interests of justice. Violation is punishable with imprisonment of up to two years and fine.

queries.query: What are the provisions for witnesses called by Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may at any stage of any inquiry or trial examine any person if his evidence appears to be essential to the just decision of the case.

queries.query: What is the procedure regarding juvenile offenders?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any offence not punishable with death or imprisonment for life, committed by any person who at the date of commission was under sixteen years of age, may be tried by a Chief Judicial Magistrate.

queries.query: What is the meaning of officer in charge of a police station?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Officer in charge of a police station means the officer in charge of a police station, and in relation to a period during which no such officer is in charge, includes any police officer present at the station.

queries.query: What is the power to detain for investigation beyond 24 hours?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate may authorize detention in judicial custody for fifteen days at a time, for a total of up to sixty days or ninety days depending on the offence.

queries.query: What is the procedure for trial of offences relating to marriage?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No Court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under Sections 493 to 496 of the Indian Penal Code without a complaint made by some person aggrieved.

queries.query: What is the procedure when accused cannot be found?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A police officer may, when there is not sufficient evidence to justify forwarding the accused to a Magistrate, release the accused on executing a bond to appear when required.

queries.query: What are the provisions for compulsory retirement for absconding?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a proclamation for attendance of any person is published under Section 82, the Court may attach any property belonging to such person.

queries.query: What is the police diary?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every investigation shall maintain a case diary, and the Court may send for police diaries of a case under inquiry or trial for examination.

queries.query: What are the provisions for evidence of government scientific experts?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any document purporting to be a report under the hand of a Government scientific expert shall be received as evidence in any inquiry trial or proceeding.

queries.query: What is the procedure regarding irregular proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If any Magistrate not empowered by law in that behalf causes a summons to issue instead of a warrant, it shall not vitiate the proceedings unless failure of justice is occasioned.

queries.query: What is the procedure when wrong court conducts trial?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A finding sentence or order of a Criminal Court shall not be set aside merely on the ground that the inquiry, trial or other proceeding took place in a wrong sessions division unless failure of justice resulted.

queries.query: What are the provisions regarding DNA tests?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A registered medical practitioner shall carry out medical examination of the accused of an offence of rape, and the report of such examination shall be signed by the medical practitioner.

queries.query: What is the procedure for grant of special leave to appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code, any person convicted on a trial held by a High Court in its extraordinary criminal jurisdiction may appeal to the Supreme Court.

queries.query: What is the procedure for investigation in chargesheet cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: As soon as investigation is completed the officer in charge of the police station shall forward to the Magistrate a police report in the prescribed form.

queries.query: What is summary dismissal of appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If upon examining the petition of appeal and copy of judgment, the Appellate Court considers that there is no sufficient ground for interfering, it may dismiss the appeal summarily.

queries.query: What is the procedure when Magistrate transfers cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Chief Judicial Magistrate may make over a case for inquiry or trial to any competent Judicial Magistrate subordinate to him.

queries.query: What are the provisions for victim compensation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every State Government shall prepare a scheme for providing funds for compensation to victims or dependants for loss or injury as a result of crime.

queries.query: What is the procedure for remand to custody?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate may authorize the detention of the accused in the custody of the police for a term not exceeding fifteen days in the whole and in judicial custody beyond fifteen days.

queries.query: What is the procedure for transfer of cases by Sessions Judge?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Sessions Judge may transfer any case for inquiry or trial from one Criminal Court to another Criminal Court in their sessions division.

queries.query: What is the procedure for disposal of criminal appeals?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Appellate Court may dismiss or allow the appeal and may pass any sentence it considers appropriate including enhancement of sentence.

queries.query: What is the procedure for maintenance of estranged wife?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A wife who has been divorced or who has obtained a divorce may apply for maintenance if she has not remarried and is unable to maintain herself.

queries.query: What is the provision regarding dying declaration?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Statements made by persons who cannot be called as witnesses are relevant facts under Section 32 of the Indian Evidence Act, including dying declarations.

queries.query: What is the procedure for challenge to prospective juror?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court may make rules prescribing procedure for the trial of cases including challenge to jurors in sessions trials.

queries.query: What is the procedure for revision by Sessions Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Sessions Court may call for and examine the record of any proceeding before any inferior Criminal Court for the purpose of satisfying itself as to the correctness of finding.

queries.query: What is the authority of Magistrate to impose sentence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A First Class Magistrate may pass a sentence of imprisonment for up to three years or fine up to ten thousand rupees or both.

queries.query: What is the procedure for cases where accused is convicted of several offences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When a person is convicted at one trial of two or more offences, the Court may pass sentences to run concurrently or consecutively.

queries.query: What is the procedure when accused pleads guilty in Sessions court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If an accused person pleads guilty to charges framed in a Sessions trial, the Judge shall record the plea and may convict the accused.

queries.query: What are the provisions for audio video recording of evidence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate or Chief Judicial Magistrate may take down the evidence in the form of questions and answers with the assistance of technology if available.

queries.query: What is the power of sessions court on revision?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In exercise of its powers of revision the Court of Session may examine the record of any proceeding before any inferior criminal court and pass such orders as may be appropriate.

queries.query: What is the procedure for calling records from subordinate courts?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court or Sessions Court may send for record and may exercise any power conferred on them, in any proceedings which is not yet decided by the Court below.

queries.query: What are the rights of an accused person in a criminal trial?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The accused has the right to be defended by a pleader of their choice, the right to be present when evidence is taken, and the right to free legal aid when unable to afford a lawyer.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied before a Magistrate can authorize detention beyond 24 hours?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The offence must be cognizable, the police officer must make a report, and the Magistrate must be satisfied there is good cause for further detention.

queries.query: What are the conditions for granting anticipatory bail under Section 438?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must consider the nature of the accusation, antecedents of the applicant, possibility of the applicant fleeing justice, and whether accusation appears to be made with mala fide intention.

queries.query: When can police arrest without warrant under Section 41?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When a person has been concerned in a cognizable offence or against whom reasonable complaint has been received or credible information exists, and the police officer has reasonable grounds to believe the arrest is necessary.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for compounding of offences under Section 320?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Certain offences may be compounded by the aggrieved person; for some offences Court permission is required; compounding bars further proceedings for the same offence.

queries.query: Under what conditions can the High Court exercise its inherent powers under Section 482?
queries.ground_truth_answer: To give effect to any order under the Code, to prevent abuse of process of any Court, or to secure the ends of justice — these are the three limbs of inherent powers.

queries.query: What are the conditions for granting bail in a non-bailable offence under Section 437?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Bail may be granted unless there appear reasonable grounds for believing the person is guilty of an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment; additional conditions apply for persons accused of serious offences.

queries.query: What conditions must be met before a Court can withdraw a prosecution under Section 321?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Public Prosecutor must apply for withdrawal with Court consent; the Court must consider whether withdrawal would be in the public interest and whether it amounts to abuse of process.

queries.query: What are the mandatory requirements for a valid charge under Section 211?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The charge must state the offence with which the accused is charged; if the offence has a specific name it must be used; the section of law must be mentioned; and it must be read and explained to the accused.

queries.query: What conditions justify remand to police custody under Section 167?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The officer must produce the accused before the Magistrate, show that the offence is cognizable, that the investigation cannot be completed in 24 hours, and that there are grounds for believing the accusation is well-founded.

queries.query: When can a Magistrate discharge an accused in a warrant case?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When the charge is groundless, or when no case has been made out which if unrebutted would warrant conviction, considering documents, statements, and examination of accused.

queries.query: What conditions are required for joinder of charges under Section 218 and 220?
queries.ground_truth_answer: For distinct offences, separate charges are required; but when acts form part of the same transaction or are so connected as to form the same transaction, a single charge may suffice.

queries.query: Under what conditions can a Court exercise revisional jurisdiction under Section 397?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may exercise revision when it appears the finding, sentence or order of the lower court is incorrect, illegal, improper, or when there was an irregularity in procedure causing failure of justice.

queries.query: What conditions justify an order under Section 144 in urgent cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: There must be sufficient ground for proceeding, the case must be urgent, there must be sufficient cause for immediate prevention or speedy remedy, and the order must be necessary to prevent public nuisance or danger.

queries.query: What is the procedure for trial when accused is absconding?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Evidence may be taken in the absence of the accused if the accused has absconded and there is no immediate prospect of arresting them; such evidence forms part of the record on subsequent arrest.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for grant of pardon under Section 306?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The pardon is for an accomplice who makes a full and true disclosure of the whole circumstances of the offence; failure to comply leads to trial for the original offence.

queries.query: What safeguards apply when police record statements under Section 161?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Oral examination is permitted but statements cannot be signed by the witness; they can only be used to contradict the witness in Court, not as substantive evidence.

queries.query: Under what conditions can the Court take cognizance on a complaint after a police report?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate must inquire into the complaint and the case shall proceed as per the police report; trial on the complaint shall not proceed except jointly with trial on the police report.

queries.query: What conditions apply for attachment of property of absconder under Section 83?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Attachment may be ordered only after a proclamation has been published; property belonging to the absconder may be attached before or after the proclamation.

queries.query: What conditions must be met before a Court orders security for good behaviour?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The person must have been convicted of offences relating to property or habitual receipt of stolen property; the period shall not exceed three years.

queries.query: What are the conditions for exercising inherent powers to quash FIR?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may quash an FIR when the allegations do not constitute a cognizable offence, the allegation is manifestly absurd, or continuing proceedings would be abuse of process.

queries.query: What conditions justify transfer of a case from one Court to another?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Transfer is justified when there is reasonable apprehension that justice will not be obtained, where there is danger of a disturbance of peace, or for administrative convenience.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied before pronouncing sentence of death?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Death sentence passed by Court of Session requires confirmation by the High Court; the Court must give an opportunity to the accused to be heard before confirmation.

queries.query: What are the safeguards for confession made before a Magistrate under Section 164?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate must warn the person that they are not bound to make a confession, must be satisfied the confession is voluntary, and must record that the warning was given and the reason for believing it is voluntary.

queries.query: What conditions justify examination of accused under Section 313?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may examine the accused to enable them to explain circumstances appearing in evidence; the examination is without oath and answers cannot be used as substantive evidence but may be considered.

queries.query: What conditions apply for release on bail pending appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A convicted person must file an appeal; the Court may order suspension of sentence and release on bail if it thinks fit having regard to the nature and gravity of offence and the character of the appellant.

queries.query: What conditions justify revision of acquittal by High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court may revise an acquittal but cannot convert it to a conviction in exercise of revisional powers; it may direct re-trial or further inquiry by the lower court.

queries.query: When can a second appeal lie in a criminal case?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A convicted person may file an appeal to the High Court against conviction on any ground; a second appeal ordinarily does not lie but a special leave appeal to Supreme Court is available.

queries.query: What conditions apply for giving compensation under Section 357?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Compensation may be ordered when a person is convicted; it may be directed to be paid out of fine, or by way of a separate compensation order when sentence is one of imprisonment.

queries.query: What are the conditions for invoking double jeopardy under Section 300?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The person must have been previously tried by a Court of competent jurisdiction; the offence must be the same or substantially the same on the same facts; the trial must have resulted in conviction or acquittal.

queries.query: What conditions justify maintenance order under Section 125?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The person liable must have sufficient means; the wife must be unable to maintain herself; the child must be illegitimate or legitimate; and there must be neglect or refusal to maintain.

queries.query: What conditions must the Court satisfy before exercising power under Section 482 to prevent abuse?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The abuse of process must be clear from the record; the proceedings must be oppressive; and the Court must be satisfied that quashing will not affect a legitimate prosecution.

queries.query: What are the conditions for summary trial under Section 260?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The offence must be in the list specified in Section 260; the Magistrate must be empowered to try summarily; and the case must not involve a sentence exceeding three months imprisonment.

queries.query: What conditions justify postponement of hearing under Section 309?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Postponement is permitted when a witness is unavailable, when the accused is absent, or when it is necessary to obtain evidence; the reason must be recorded.

queries.query: What conditions apply for attachment of property under Section 82 and 83?
queries.ground_truth_answer: There must be reason to believe the person has absconded; property may be attached before or after proclamation; the attachment may be executed anywhere within India.

queries.query: What conditions justify issuing a search warrant under Section 94?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must have reason to believe that a document or thing cannot be produced by a summons, or the document is not known to be in any person's possession, or inspection of a place is necessary.

queries.query: What conditions apply for trial in absence of accused under Section 317?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may dispense with attendance if accused is ill, if personal attendance causes undue hardship, or if the pleader appears on their behalf, except when judgment is to be pronounced.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for a Court to release a person on probation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The offender must not have been previously convicted of a similar offence; the offence must not be punishable with death or life imprisonment; and the Court must consider it expedient.

queries.query: What conditions apply for a Court to transfer a case to try jointly?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Two offences may be tried together when they form the same transaction; or when multiple offences form a series of acts of the same kind within twelve months.

queries.query: What conditions justify a Court calling for additional evidence on appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Appellate Court may record additional evidence when it is necessary for proper disposal of the appeal; it may do so itself or direct the lower Court to record it.

queries.query: What are the conditions for grant of police custody remand?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Police custody can be authorized only in the first fifteen days of detention; thereafter the accused must be in judicial custody; total detention cannot exceed sixty or ninety days.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for taking cognizance of offences by Courts of Session?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Court of Session shall not take cognizance of an offence unless the accused has been committed to it by a Magistrate under the provisions of the Code.

queries.query: What conditions justify an order for medical examination under Section 53?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When a person is arrested for an offence and there are reasonable grounds to believe that an examination of his person will afford evidence of the commission of an offence, examination may be ordered.

queries.query: What conditions are required for taking cognizance on a private complaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate must examine the complainant on oath; must be satisfied there is sufficient ground; may postpone issue of process to make inquiry; and may dismiss the complaint if frivolous.

queries.query: What conditions apply to grant of legal aid under Section 304?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The accused must not be represented by a pleader; the Court must be of opinion that the circumstances of the case and interests of justice require assignment of a pleader.

queries.query: What conditions justify commitment to Court of Session?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The offence must be exclusively triable by the Court of Session; the Magistrate must be satisfied there is prima facie ground to proceed; and the accused must be present or have appeared.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied before passing an order under Section 133?
