queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate must be satisfied on report of a police officer or other information; must state the circumstances if existence of right is denied; and must give the party an opportunity to be heard.

queries.query: What conditions justify the prosecution's right to adduce further evidence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: On completion of investigation the officer files a chargesheet; the prosecution may thereafter call any further witness even if not mentioned in the chargesheet if the Court permits.

queries.query: What conditions apply for grant of bail in cases of anticipatory arrest under Section 438?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must consider the nature and gravity of accusation, antecedents of the person, possibility of fleeing justice, and whether accusation appears to be made with intent to humiliate.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for using a confession against a co-accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A confession made by an accused affecting themselves and a co-accused, tried jointly, may be taken into account against the co-accused but it is a weak piece of evidence.

queries.query: What conditions apply to revision of order of maintenance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Maintenance order may be varied on proof of change in circumstances of the payer or the recipient; marriage of the divorced wife is a ground for cancellation.

queries.query: What conditions are required for a proclamation to be valid under Section 82?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The person must have been summoned, the summons must have been served or shown to be ineffective, and there must be reason to believe the person is absconding or concealing themselves.

queries.query: What conditions justify refusing bail to a person accused of a heinous offence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Bail may be refused when there are reasonable grounds for believing the person is guilty of an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment; prior convictions; and reasonable ground for believing the person is a habitual offender.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for the police to record a dying declaration?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The dying declaration may be recorded by a police officer under Section 161 but it has limited evidentiary value; a dying declaration recorded by a Magistrate under Section 164 has greater weight.

queries.query: What conditions justify the Court taking cognizance of an offence committed by a judge or public servant?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Previous sanction of the Government is required for prosecution of a judge or public servant acting or purporting to act in discharge of their official duties.

queries.query: What conditions justify enforcement of an order of maintenance under Section 128?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Court in any part of India enforcing the order shall have the same power as the Court which made it; the person in default may be imprisoned for up to one month for each breach.

queries.query: What conditions apply to evidence obtained through illegal search?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Evidence obtained through an illegal search is not automatically excluded but the Court may consider the illegality when evaluating the evidence and it affects the weight to be given.

queries.query: What conditions are required for a plea of autrefois acquit to succeed?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The offence must be the same or substantially the same as the previous charge; the previous acquittal must be by a competent Court; and the trial must have concluded with a final order.

queries.query: What conditions justify a Magistrate postponing proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate may postpone when a witness is unavailable, when the accused cannot attend due to illness, or when it is necessary to obtain evidence — but reasons must be recorded.

queries.query: What conditions apply for taking cognizance of private complaint after dismissal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where the complaint is dismissed the complainant may file a revision; fresh complaint on same facts after dismissal is generally not maintainable unless new facts have emerged.

queries.query: What conditions justify sending a case back for re-investigation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate may direct further investigation on finding the police report incomplete; the investigating officer may also conduct further investigation at any time.

queries.query: What conditions apply for the Magistrate to issue a warrant instead of a summons?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A warrant may be issued instead of a summons when the accused is likely to abscond or when a summons would not bring the accused before the Court.

queries.query: What conditions must be met before passing an order for victim compensation under Section 357A?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The State scheme must be in place; the victim must be unable to be identified or the offender untraced; the recommendation of the Court to the Legal Services Authority is needed.

queries.query: What conditions apply to revision of sentence by High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court may enhance a sentence in revision but must give the accused an opportunity to show cause against enhancement; it cannot exercise this power to convert acquittal to conviction.

queries.query: What conditions justify conviction on the basis of sole testimony of prosecutrix?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Courts may convict on the sole testimony of prosecutrix if it is reliable and credible; corroboration is a rule of prudence not of law in sexual offences.

queries.query: What conditions apply to remanding of juvenile accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Juvenile accused may be tried only by a Chief Judicial Magistrate or a Magistrate specially empowered; the procedure differs and reformative approach is mandated.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied before passing a sentence of imprisonment in default of fine?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The term of imprisonment in default must not exceed one fourth of the maximum term of imprisonment for the offence; it cannot exceed the powers of the court.

queries.query: What conditions justify setting aside a forfeiture of bond under Section 446?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The person who executed the bond may apply for reduction or setting aside; the Court must be satisfied that there was sufficient cause for non-appearance.

queries.query: What conditions apply to conviction for a lesser offence when greater offence is charged?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When the Court finds the accused not guilty of the offence charged but guilty of a lesser offence included within the charge, it may convict for the lesser offence.

queries.query: What are the conditions under which a Court may discharge an accused in a Sessions trial?
queries.ground_truth_answer: After hearing arguments if the Judge considers that there is not sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, the Judge shall discharge the accused and record reasons.

queries.query: What conditions justify a Magistrate taking cognizance suo motu?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Magistrate may take cognizance upon information received from any person other than a police officer; the exercise of power must be bona fide and not used to harass.

queries.query: What conditions apply to grant of bail after conviction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must take into account the nature of the offence, the character of the evidence, and the circumstances of the case when granting bail pending appeal.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for an order of costs in criminal proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Costs can be awarded against a complainant who falsely or frivolously prosecutes; they can also be awarded as compensation where acquittal results from false charges.

queries.query: What conditions apply to trial when accused is mentally ill?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If the accused appears to be unable to understand proceedings due to unsoundness of mind the proceedings shall be postponed; the accused may be released on bail or sent to custody.

queries.query: What conditions justify a Court taking up revision even without an application?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court may on its own motion call for records and exercise revision powers; this power is preventive and corrective and not a substitute for appeal.

queries.query: What conditions are required before a police officer can break open a door for arrest?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The police officer must be authorized to arrest the person; the officer must notify their authority and purpose; and must have been refused admittance or unable to obtain admittance.

queries.query: What conditions apply for maintaining of register of cases under Section 154?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every FIR must be registered; a copy must be given to the informant free of cost; any refusal to register may be complained to the Superintendent of Police.

queries.query: What conditions must exist for the Court to hear an appeal against acquittal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Leave must be obtained from the High Court; the appeal must show that the acquittal was perverse or clearly unreasonable; the High Court exercises limited power.

queries.query: What conditions justify examination of accused at end of prosecution evidence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court shall put to the accused all incriminating circumstances in evidence for explanation; failure to do so vitiates the conviction if prejudice is caused.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the power of police officer to make arrest under exigent circumstances?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A police officer may arrest any person who designs to commit a cognizable offence if it cannot be otherwise prevented; such person shall be detained only until the danger of commission is over.

queries.query: What conditions justify issuing a non-bailable warrant for first appearance of accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Court may issue a warrant instead of summons when it has reason to believe the accused will not obey the summons or when such issue appears to be necessary.

queries.query: What conditions apply for the Court to permit prosecution by private party?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may permit any person to appear as prosecutor in a case; the Public Prosecutor may also assist such prosecution; the prosecution must be conducted lawfully.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for an application for review of judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Court cannot alter or review a judgment once signed; but may correct clerical or arithmetical errors and no application for review lies in criminal proceedings except against orders on bail.

queries.query: What conditions justify a Magistrate ordering the accused to furnish security?
queries.ground_truth_answer: There must be reasonable grounds to believe the person is likely to commit a breach of peace or is a habitual offender; the bond must be for a definite period not exceeding three years.

queries.query: What conditions apply for prosecution of a company for a criminal offence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A company or other body corporate may be charged with and convicted of an offence; a representative must be present to answer on behalf of the company.

queries.query: What conditions justify taking cognizance on basis of police report?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Cognizance may be taken on a police report if it discloses a cognizable offence; the Magistrate must apply their judicial mind to determine if the report makes out a case.

queries.query: What conditions apply to taking cognizance by Special Courts?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Special Courts created under special laws take cognizance in accordance with their enabling statute; the Code of Criminal Procedure applies to the extent not inconsistent.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right of accused to cross-examine prosecution witnesses?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The accused has a right to cross-examine every witness for the prosecution; this right is fundamental; denial of adequate opportunity may result in reversal of conviction.

queries.query: What conditions justify a Court acquitting an accused after defence evidence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: After the prosecution evidence a Court of Session shall acquit if it finds no grounds to proceed; acquittal should follow when there is no probability of conviction on the total evidence.

queries.query: What conditions apply to a Magistrate committing a case to Sessions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate must be satisfied that the offence is exclusively triable by Sessions; must commit after examining the documents and hearing the parties.

queries.query: What conditions justify exercise of discretion by High Court in bail matters?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court exercises discretion considering the seriousness of offence, antecedents, flight risk, possibility of tampering with evidence, and period of detention.

queries.query: What conditions apply to enhancement of sentence by appellate court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Appellate Court may enhance a sentence on appeal by the State; accused must be given an opportunity to show cause; the Court must give reasons.

queries.query: What conditions must exist for a Magistrate to order attachment of disputed property?
queries.ground_truth_answer: There must be likelihood of breach of peace; the Magistrate must be unable to determine which party is in possession; attachment is interim pending final order.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the prosecution of offences against the state?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Previous sanction of the Government is required for prosecution of offences under Chapters VI and VIII of IPC; the sanction must be applied for before cognizance is taken.

queries.query: What conditions justify the Magistrate recording further statement under Section 164?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate may record a statement or confession at any stage of the investigation; must ensure the person is not in police custody and the statement is voluntary.

queries.query: What conditions apply to release of under trial prisoner on bail by default?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A person who has been in custody for half the maximum period of imprisonment for the offence shall be released on bail; this provision applies to under-trial prisoners.

queries.query: What conditions must exist before the Court pronounces judgment of conviction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The judgment must contain the point or points for determination, the decision thereon, and the reasons for the decision; must be written in the language of the court.

queries.query: What conditions justify allowing a revision of conviction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must be satisfied that there is an error in law or fact; the proceedings must show illegality; the revision court cannot re-appreciate evidence in the same manner as an appellate court.

queries.query: What conditions apply to trial of juvenile for heinous offence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Juvenile Justice law prevails; the Court must determine whether the child can be tried as an adult based on mental capacity and physical capacity to commit the offence.

queries.query: What conditions justify a police officer's power to disperse riotous assembly?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Executive Magistrate or police may use civilian force; use of armed force requires order from Magistrate; minimum force proportionate to the threat must be used.

queries.query: What conditions apply to execution of sentence of fine?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Fine may be recovered by warrant of attachment and sale of movable property; imprisonment in default of fine runs concurrently with substantive sentence.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for declaring a person habitual offender?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The person must have been convicted of offences relating to habitual receipt of stolen property or habitually commits extortion or habitually commits offences under special laws.

queries.query: What conditions justify bail to a person accused of an economic offence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Economic offences are treated differently; Courts must consider the gravity of the offence, the role of the accused, and the loss caused to public before granting bail.

queries.query: What conditions apply to trial of offences against children under special provisions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every hospital must provide free first aid or medical treatment to victims of crimes against children; the victim is entitled to compensation under victim compensation scheme.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right of police to obtain voice samples from accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Courts may direct the accused to give voice samples for the purpose of investigation; refusal by accused may be noted by the Court as evidence of guilty conscience.

queries.query: What conditions justify extension of time in investigation under Section 167?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Extension of time beyond 60 days requires that the offence be punishable with death, imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment for at least 10 years; otherwise the accused gets bail.

queries.query: What conditions apply to forfeiture of recognizance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The surety or the accused must show cause; the Court may remit the forfeiture; the Court must be satisfied that the surety acted in good faith.

queries.query: What are the mandatory requirements for a judgment in a criminal trial under Section 354?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Judgment must be pronounced in open court; must contain the offence proved, evidence considered, and reasons for the decision; must be signed by the Judge.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied before a Court makes a reference to the High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must have doubt on a question of law; the question must be necessary for disposal of the case; the case must be pending before the Court.

queries.query: What conditions justify attachment of property of a foreign national under Section 83?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The provisions apply equally to foreign nationals; attachment may be affected within India; recovery from foreign property requires following treaty provisions.

queries.query: What conditions apply to cancellation of bail granted by Sessions Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: High Court may cancel bail granted by Sessions Court if there is misuse of liberty, apprehension of tampering with evidence, or if the order granting bail is perverse.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for granting bail to a person accused under NDPS Act?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Stringent conditions apply under NDPS Act; bail should be refused unless there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty and will not commit any offence while on bail.

queries.query: What conditions apply to a search of premises without a warrant under Section 165?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The officer must have reasonable grounds to believe that delay in obtaining a warrant would result in concealment of evidence; must leave a copy of grounds at the searched place.

queries.query: What conditions justify stay of proceedings by High Court under Section 482?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court may stay proceedings if they are vexatious, oppressive, or an abuse of process; interim stay may be granted on a prima facie case being made out.

queries.query: What conditions apply to recording of statement of child witness?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Statement of child victim must be recorded by Magistrate; in camera proceedings may be ordered; child must not be made to face the accused during recording.

queries.query: What conditions justify taking cognizance of contempt of court in criminal proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No Court shall take cognizance of offences relating to giving false evidence unless there is a complaint in writing by the Court; the offence must occur in judicial proceedings.

queries.query: What conditions apply to non-compoundable offences being settled informally?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Non-compoundable offences cannot be settled by the parties; the State prosecution must continue; however in matrimonial matters the Supreme Court may exercise Article 142 powers.

queries.query: What conditions justify granting bail when trial is not concluded in time?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If investigation or trial is not completed within the prescribed period the accused becomes entitled to bail as of right; the accused must not have previously availed of this right.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied before a Magistrate orders maintenance under Section 125?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The spouse or child must be unable to maintain themselves; the person liable must have sufficient means; there must be neglect or refusal to maintain; the applicant must fall within eligible categories.

queries.query: What conditions apply to award of compensation from State under Section 357A?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The State scheme must provide for compensation; trial court may recommend compensation; Legal Services Authority decides quantum; victim includes legal heirs.

queries.query: What conditions justify a Magistrate directing further investigation after chargesheet?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Courts may direct further investigation when the chargesheet is incomplete, when new evidence has emerged, or when the investigation is unsatisfactory.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right of convicted person to appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An appeal lies as of right from a conviction by Sessions Judge to High Court and from High Court in original jurisdiction to Supreme Court; special leave to appeal is available against all orders.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied before exercising power to enhance sentence in appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The appellate court must give notice to the accused to show cause; enhancement must be proportionate to the gravity of offence; sentence should not exceed the maximum prescribed.

queries.query: What conditions justify quashing proceedings against company as accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A company accused of a criminal offence may be convicted and sentenced to fine; imprisonment cannot be imposed on a company; company must act through its representative.

queries.query: What conditions apply to bail in case of offences against women?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Courts are directed to be more liberal in granting bail to women accused; however in serious offences against women the accused may not be entitled to bail readily.

queries.query: What conditions justify the Magistrate issuing notice to state before deciding bail?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In anticipatory bail applications the prosecution must be heard; the Public Prosecutor may oppose the application; the Court must record reasons for granting or rejecting bail.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the power of police to search vehicle at a checkpoint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Police may search any person or vehicle if there is reasonable suspicion; the officer must record grounds of search; a copy of the grounds must be given to the person searched.

queries.query: What conditions justify revision of sentence to provide for suspension?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The power to suspend is available during appeal; the State power to remit under Section 432 is separate; Courts must not use revision as a substitute for appeal.

queries.query: What conditions must exist for a Magistrate to pass an order under Section 144 against a named individual?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Magistrate must have cogent reasons; the threat must be immediate; the order must be specific about what is prohibited; the order must be served on the person named.

queries.query: What conditions apply to extension of the total period of detention beyond 60 days?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Under the proviso to Section 167(2), where the investigation cannot be completed within 60 days the Magistrate may authorise continued detention up to 90 days where the offence is punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than 10 years; for all other offences the maximum total period is 60 days. If the chargesheet is not filed within the applicable period the accused is entitled to bail as of right.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for recording evidence through video conferencing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The accused must be able to see and hear the witness and vice versa; the accused must be able to cross-examine the witness; the record must be made available to the accused.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the power of the police to handcuff an accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The power to handcuff is discretionary; it should only be used when there is a genuine apprehension of escape; the handcuffing must be reported to the Court on production.

queries.query: What conditions justify an interim order restraining disposal of assets pending investigation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The police officer may seize any property found under circumstances which create suspicion of commission of an offence; the property must be reported to the Magistrate promptly.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the reading of evidence to an illiterate accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: All evidence taken must be read over and explained to the accused; if unable to understand the language the evidence must be interpreted; the accused must be given an opportunity to reply.

queries.query: What conditions must be met before passing a sentence of fine only without imprisonment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court has discretion to impose only fine where the offence provides for alternative of fine; the Court must give reasons; the imprisonment in default must be within the powers of the court.

queries.query: How do Sections 82 and 83 together provide for dealing with absconders?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 82 provides for proclamation requiring absconders to appear; Section 83 enables attachment of their property; together they form a complete mechanism to compel appearance.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Sections 190 and 193 in taking cognizance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 190 governs cognizance by Magistrates; Section 193 governs cognizance by Sessions Courts which requires committal by Magistrate; both define the threshold for initiation of trial.

queries.query: How do Sections 154 and 173 define the beginning and end of police investigation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 154 mandates registration of FIR marking commencement of investigation; Section 173 requires filing of chargesheet on completion; together they define the investigation lifecycle.

queries.query: How do Sections 378 and 386 govern State appeal against acquittal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 378 gives the State the right to appeal against acquittal; Section 386 defines the powers of the Appellate Court in allowing or dismissing appeals including those by the State.

queries.query: What is the interplay between Sections 313 and 315 regarding examination of accused?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 313 enables examination of accused by Court to explain incriminating evidence; Section 315 enables the accused to be a competent witness in their own defence; both deal with accused's voice in trial.

queries.query: How do Sections 432 and 433 differ in the power to deal with sentences?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 432 provides power to suspend or remit sentences; Section 433 provides power to commute sentences from one nature to another; together they give the Executive complete power to modify sentences.

queries.query: How do Sections 227 and 232 provide for discharge or acquittal at different stages?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 227 enables discharge before framing of charge if no sufficient ground; Section 232 enables acquittal after prosecution evidence before accused is called for defence if no case is made out.

queries.query: How do Sections 395 and 401 provide for reference and revision by High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 395 enables subordinate Courts to make reference on question of law; Section 401 enables High Court to exercise revisional powers on its own motion; both are supervisory mechanisms.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Sections 300 and 320 regarding protection from double prosecution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 300 bars second trial for same offence after conviction or acquittal; Section 320 provides compounding which also bars further prosecution; both protect against double jeopardy.

queries.query: How do Sections 306 and 307 work together for tendering pardon?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 306 empowers Chief Judicial Magistrate to tender pardon; Section 307 empowers the Court of Session or High Court to direct the Magistrate to tender pardon; they define who can tender and who can direct.

queries.query: How do Sections 357 and 357A together provide for victim compensation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 357 empowers Courts to order compensation from fines; Section 357A provides for State-funded compensation scheme where offender is untraceable; together they form a comprehensive victim reparation framework.

queries.query: How do Sections 97 and 100 provide for search for persons wrongfully confined?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 97 provides for search warrant to search for persons wrongfully confined; Section 100 provides for search of place entered by persons sought to be arrested; both deal with physical search.

queries.query: How do Sections 107 and 111 operate together in security proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 107 provides for security for keeping the peace; Section 111 provides the procedure for making the order requiring appearance and show cause; together they define the security proceeding mechanism.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Sections 161 and 164 in recording of statements?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 161 governs oral examination by police; Section 164 governs recording of confessions and statements by Magistrate; the latter carries more evidentiary weight than the former.

queries.query: How do Sections 200 and 204 work in complaint cases before Magistrate?
